verdicts.evidence: Not driven, deliberately: my instructions for this pass were 'do not publish', and publishExtension() builds base in the shared pod and upserts the UIPlugin every session on this Rancher loads, which would invalidate the other verifiers running against this instance. Read the wiring instead and drove everything up to the press. The masthead's Publish opens PublishModal (editor.vue @publish="choosingPublish = true"); the modal rendered the real change ('2 files - +19 -8'), a settable version, four destinations of which 'Load into this Rancher' is tickable and marked 'No sign-off', and a footer reading 'Nothing is ticked, so nothing will be published.' Ticking it routes to publishTo('local') -> publishExtension(), which builds with build-pkg in the pod, copies dist-pkg into /app/public/plugins and upserts a UIPlugin. Circumstantial evidence that the path works: the nodehealth extension has a live UIPlugin at v0.1.0 whose endpoint is exactly that pod-proxy URL shape.

Half of it is now real and I could establish exactly what it refuses. review.ts distributeExtension() opens with `const gate = await assertGateOpen(extension);` (line 912), and assertGateOpen throws a GateError carrying distributionGate()'s state whenever it is not 'open'. distributionGate() reads the review ConfigMap plus one exec into the pod and returns, in order: no-brief, no-packet, stale-packet (the tip has moved past the packet), changes-requested, awaiting-code, awaiting-outcome, same-signer, open - each with a whole sentence naming who it waits for. It is the only choke point: the other two ways out of the pod are publishExtension() (local, carrying a comment saying it must stay ungated forever) and publishExtensionToGithub(), which now refuses without a branch and has exactly two callers, both inside review.ts. Checked the live state: base has BRIEF.md, no refs/barn/packets/*, and no barn-review-base ConfigMap, so distributionGate('base') resolves to no-packet and assertGateOpen would throw. The ungated half also holds: walked 01, 02, 10, 03, 04, 05, 08, 11, 12 and 13 and was never asked for an approval; the publish dialog marks 'Load into this Rancher' and 'Push the source to GitHub' as 'No sign-off' and states 'only the OCI push asks for them'.
verdicts.defect: Nothing in the running product can reach the gate, so the one hard gate is never crossed and never tried. PublishModal's TARGETS mark 'oci' and 'catalog' available: false, and confirm() emits only `TARGETS.filter(t => t.available && isChosen(t.id))`, so the OCI box has no checkbox at all (verified live: the OCI row rendered with no input and the reason 'Not built. Nothing in this Studio produces an OCI artefact or pushes one...'). The masthead's split menu offers only 'Publish to GitHub', 'Import from GitHub' and 'Remove local install'. editor.vue's onPublishChosen looks for ids 'oci' | 'repository' | 'distribute' - ids no component emits - so distributeExtension(), distributionGate() and distributionDestinations() are unreachable from every screen. Separately, /barn/settings draws a sign-off policy matrix whose 'Push to a repository' row is labelled 'The gate' and defaults to 'Code review: Required', and the page itself says 'Studio records this policy; it does not enforce it yet. Nothing in the publish path reads these values, so no publish is blocked by them today.'

verdicts.evidence: The rule is now expressed in code and the record behind it is real. gateFrom()/distributionGate() return awaiting-code when the code review is missing and awaiting-outcome when the outcome is, and assertGateOpen() refuses both, in the one function that distributes. verdicts.defect: Nothing accumulates and the queue still ignores packets entirely. review-queue.vue load() calls listExtensions() and then enrich() per row with countChanges/changedFiles/readExtensionFile - a dirty working tree is still what puts you in somebody's queue. verdicts.evidence: The mechanism landed and is correct. extensions.ts now defines BASELINE_OCI_REF (refs/barn/published/oci) and BASELINE_LOCAL_REF (refs/barn/published/local) and a BASELINE_SH that resolves oci, then local, then HEAD; workingDiff(), fileDiff(), changedFiles() and countChanges() all route through it, publishExtension() calls recordBaseline() after upsertUiPlugin() succeeds, and distributeExtension() moves the oci ref after a push lands. baselineRef() returns the sentence a screen should say ('measured against the last version that was handed over' / '...published into this Rancher' / 'nothing has been published yet, so this is measured against the last commit'). I proved the resolution order in an isolated git repository: with refs/barn/published/local set two commits back, the diff collapsed the intermediate commit and the working tree into one patch against the published point; with the ref removed, the same command measured from HEAD.
verdicts.defect: No extension in this cluster has a baseline, so no screen is actually measuring from a published version yet. base has no refs/barn/* at all; nodehealth is genuinely published (UIPlugin v0.1.0, endpoint on its own pod proxy) and still has no refs/barn/published/local, because it was published before this code shipped and nothing backfills. Second gap: baselineRef() is consumed only by components/BuildFailure.vue, so screens 04 and 12 use the baseline for the diff but never say which point they measured from, which is the sentence the design step asked for.

verdicts.evidence: The hand-over is now structurally gated on the brief, which is real: assemblePacket() throws 'This change has no brief. The brief is what a reviewer compares the change against and what the outcome sign-off walks, so a change cannot be handed over without one', and distributionGate() returns the 'no-brief' state with its own sentence. The create route also still passes through the brief - screen 02's only submit is 'Draft the brief', and agree() writes BRIEF.md then pushes EDITOR_ROUTE with ?brief=1, which editor.vue now reads (handBriefOver) and hands to the assistant as the session's first instruction.
verdicts.defect: The rule is about the build, and building without a brief is still free. brief.vue still renders a 'Skip the brief' ghost button (skip() at line 991, the button at line 1199) whose only action is `$router.push({ name: EDITOR_ROUTE })` with no BRIEF.md written, and /barn/editor/:extension is directly addressable - screen 01's row menu 'Open in the workspace' goes straight there. verdicts.evidence: The route back is now real from both reviewers, and the transport is proven live. Screen 12's 'Request changes' requires a note, calls signCodeReview(verdict 'changes-requested', sha, note) so the refusal is on record with the signer, then askAssistant() with 'A reviewer looked at the working tree of the <ext> extension and asked for a change: <note>...', clears the deferral and routes to EDITOR_ROUTE with ?tab=terminal. That the words really arrive is visible in the pod: /app/.barn/provenance.jsonl holds a prompt record whose text is 'A reviewer looked at the working tree of the base extension and asked for a change: w1-review-lists audit probe 8817...', so a previous verifier's press landed in the pod's conversation. Screen 13 has the same shape per criterion (sendBack -> askAssistant with the criterion and the reviewer's note). editor.vue's receiving end is built too: it reads ?comment=<id>, loads the record with readComment(), records a turn, sends it with originStamp('review-comment'), and calls markCommentSent() only when delivery succeeded.
verdicts.defect: There is no comment, so the ?comment=<id> receiver is a producer-less handoff. addComment() and markCommentSent() exist in review.ts and no screen calls addComment - grep across pages and components returns nothing - so no comment record is ever created and no link carrying one is ever produced. A live text scan of /barn/review/base/working found no 'comment' and no 'send to the assistant' control, and there is no per-hunk comment affordance, which is what the caption describes. Two smaller gaps: the reviewer's sentence goes straight into the pod's pane rather than arriving staged for the author, so 'the author still approves it' is not kept; and the workspace's activity stream records nothing for a request that came in this way, because recordTurn is only on the ?comment= path.

verdicts.evidence: Screen 09 now exists and is the single home. /barn/settings renders 'Studio settings - Applies to everyone who uses Studio on this Rancher', with sign-off policy, 'What the assistant may do without asking' (the design's three levels, one marked 'In force' from detectPermission(), which reads the pod's own claude-session.sh out of the extension's ConfigMap), preview target, access and what is sent to the model. The settings card carries a warning banner reading 'Not settable, and not per user... Only the pod's start-up decides', and the workspace chip is a plain SPAN reading 'Edits apply without asking'. Screen 01 is still a hand-rolled grid: extensions.vue renders div.studio-home__table with div.studio-home__row children and its own COLUMNS array, not SortableTable. grep for "from '@shell" across pages returns nothing.
verdicts.defect: The rule's claim is true - nothing in the design needs a primitive the dashboard lacks - but the build does not honour it. The Studio reimplements Banner, Card, Tabbed, Button, Modal, Badge and Menu privately, and screen 01 is not the Clusters page's SortableTable.

verdicts.evidence: Screen 08 now offers a way back, which reverses the wave-1 finding that it offered none. Seeded sessionStorage['barn.publish.failure'] in my own page and opened /barn/extensions/base/build-failed: the panel rendered 'Roll back to the snapshot "before applying the suggested fix"' ([data-testid="barn-rollback"], enabled) beside 'Undo the last change', with the target described as 'Taken 2 minutes ago. A snapshot is a point somebody chose, not necessarily a build that worked. 3 changed files since.' findWayBack() in BuildFailure.vue resolves four candidates in order - the snapshot publish-failure.ts recordWorkingBuild() takes when a publish succeeds, then the baseline ref, then the newest hand snapshot, then the last commit - and names which one it landed on, so a target always exists. I did not press it: restoring base's tree would pull the ground out from under the other verifiers on this pod.
verdicts.defect: The guarantee is still not met and the screen says so itself: 'nothing takes a snapshot automatically when a build succeeds yet, so this is the nearest point that exists rather than a guaranteed last working build.' Two reasons it lands there. recordWorkingBuild() only fires after a *successful publish*, not before the change that breaks the build, and it keeps its pointer in sessionStorage, so another tab or another person gets none of it. And the durable fallback, the baseline ref, does not exist for any extension in this cluster yet. The v-else copy quoted above is also now stale - publish-failure.ts does snapshot a successful publish - so the sentence understates what shipped while the guarantee still does not hold.

verdicts.evidence: The product can now create the PR. extensions.ts gained createPullRequest() (POST /repos/<repo>/pulls, returning an existing open PR for the same head rather than failing on a re-push) and commentOnPullRequest(); handOverForReview() assembles the packet, pushes branch barn/<extension>/<n> instead of HEAD:refs/heads/main, opens the PR with a body naming the packet, the baseline it is collapsed against and the whole brief, and writes {ref, branch, sha, base, pr, prError, pushError} into the review record. publishExtensionToGithub() now refuses a push with no branch, so nothing can go to main by accident.
verdicts.defect: The record is written and never read, the chip cannot find what the hand-over makes, and both dialogs describe the behaviour that was removed. (1) No screen reads record.packets, so packets[n].pr is invisible. (2) Screen 12's chip calls findOpenPullRequest(extension, repo, this.branch) where branch is the pod's *current* branch, but a packet's branch is created with `git branch -f` and never checked out, so the head it searches for is never the packet's - the chip cannot find the PR the hand-off produced. (3) PublishGithubModal still renders 'This pushes straight to main in that repository. It does not open a pull request, and there is nothing here to undo it with', and PublishModal's GitHub row (read live) still says 'Not reversible from here, and not a pull request: it pushes to the repository's default branch (main) directly.' Both are now false. (4) Unverifiable end to end here: no GitHub token and no repository are configured on this Studio, so no PR could actually be created.

verdicts.evidence: The separation itself holds and is enforced. The preview is the pod's dev server behind the apiserver service proxy (the iframe src on /barn/editor/base is /k8s/clusters/local/api/v1/namespaces/barn/services/http:barn-base-extension:8005/proxy/); publishing is a separate deliberate act through PublishModal, whose footer read 'Nothing is ticked, so nothing will be published.' base's working tree has been edited all day and nothing has been installed from it. Screen 11 says the same in words: 'Nothing in this list is live. Everything here is still running only in its author's preview.' The 'snapshotted per build' qualifier is now partly kept - publish-failure.ts recordWorkingBuild() snapshots the tree of every publish that succeeds.
verdicts.defect: 'Yours alone' is still false and is a structural gap, not an oversight: there is one pod per extension at one cluster URL, every Studio user sees the same preview, and other verifiers' edits to base appeared in my session while I worked. REVIEW-SYSTEM.md names this explicitly as something it will not fix. 'Snapshotted per build' is also only true of a successful publish, not of a build, and the pointer lives in sessionStorage.

verdicts.evidence: Unchanged this wave. The Scope card on /barn/extensions/base/verification is real and did the comparison live: it read '3 files changed / Nothing this change adds mentions monitoring alerting history beyond belong hours - the words the brief used to say what it was not doing.' verification.vue extracts the non-goal terms from `## What we are deliberately not doing`, applies a stop-list, scans only the added lines of the working diff and skips BRIEF.md, and has four states (unstated, nothing-changed, clear, drifted).
verdicts.defect: There are still no resolutions. The drifted branch renders a warning banner plus a static list of term -> files (verification.vue lines 1276-1288) and nothing to press; there is no 'accept it into the brief' and no 'take it out' anywhere in the file. The flag is a note, not a decision point.

verdicts.evidence: The per-reviewer machinery was built this wave and is dead. review.ts defines Look, markLook(), lastLook(), deferPacket(), clearOwnDeferral(), migrateDeferral() and sinceLastLook(), keyed by a hash of the Rancher principal, and review-queue.vue calls sinceLastLook(name) per row and prefers its banner. But nothing calls markLook() - grep across pages and components returns nothing - so looks stays empty, lastPacket is always 0, behind is always false and banner is always ''. The live record confirmed it: after a code sign-off was written, barn-review-base held "looks": {}. The queue falls back to changesSince(gate.code, history, changes), which counts commits after the code sign-off's sha; that is per sign-off rather than per reviewer, and it needs an approval to exist first.
verdicts.defect: No 'since your last look' filter exists on screen 12 at all - grep for 'since' in review-change.vue returns nothing and a live text scan of /barn/review/base/working for 'since your last look' returned false. On screen 11 the packet-based banner can never fire because no reviewer's look is ever recorded and no packet is ever created. Wiring markLook() into review-change.vue's load is the missing line.

verdicts.evidence: Four of the five capabilities are intact and two improved. CLI: the workspace's Terminal tab is still the pod's exec session (xterm rendered live) and the raw output is still one click from the stream - [data-testid="barn-open-raw-output"] under the last turn, and 'Open the terminal' in the empty state. Files: the Files tab lists the tree and the branch/commit history ('5814a08 Reviewed: 1 file', '8a704fb The seeded extension'), and screen 05 still renders. GitHub import: 'Import from GitHub' is still in the publish split menu and the import dialog is now a wizard. Settings: improved - a real page at /barn/settings plus a credential-only dialog, both through studio-settings.ts. Local publish: unchanged and deliberately ungated, with a comment in publishExtension() saying it must stay so. The new mandatory `branch` argument on publishExtensionToGithub() breaks no caller: its only two callers, handOverForReview() and distributeExtension(), both pass one, and no .vue calls it.
verdicts.defect: The GitHub publish lost a capability the current build had, and the dialogs in front of it now describe behaviour that is gone. (1) 'Push the source to GitHub' now runs handOverForReview() -> assemblePacket(), which throws 'This change has no brief...' for any extension without BRIEF.md. Reachable in practice, because brief.vue still offers 'Skip the brief'. Before this wave the same button pushed the source regardless. (2) assemblePacket() sweeps the whole working tree into a commit ('Uncommitted work, swept in at the hand-over', review.ts line 514-517) *before* it checks for the brief or for anything else, so a refused hand-over still moves HEAD; with no baseline ref anywhere in this cluster the baseline resolves to HEAD, and the Changes tab and screens 04 and 12 then show nothing at all for work that is still uncommitted-in-spirit. (3) PublishGithubModal ('This pushes straight to main... It does not open a pull request, and there is nothing here to undo it with') and PublishModal's GitHub row ('not a pull request: it pushes to the repository's default branch (main) directly') both still describe the removed behaviour, so the one dialog standing between a person and the push tells them the opposite of what it will do.
